summary: Glasdegib carries the strongest type of warning from the FDA because it can cause severe birth defects or death to an unborn baby [3]. Official warnings also advise patients not to donate blood during treatment and for at least 30 days after the last dose, and to watch for changes in heart rhythm called QTc interval prolongation [3]. In addition, a study on the drug was stopped early because of side effects [6]. Small computer models, rather than tests on people, gave this drug a high risk score for the liver and a low risk score for the heart [M].
